summary.oneLiner: Record quarter on every line — highest-ever Q1 sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT — with consolidated revenue +36.6% YoY to Rs 91.79 cr and PAT +67% (EPS Rs 2.52 vs Rs 1.50), achieved *despite* war-driven consumable inflation (carbide tools +300%) that they fully absorbed. The growth story is now explicitly export/China+1-led: a June US/Canada roadshow (Magna, Allison, Linamar) generated RFQs/NDAs worth an incremental Rs 65-75 cr over FY27-28, on top of a Rs 75 cr domestic RFQ pipeline (75-80% strike). Brakes surprised with 25% EBITDA (vs 12-14% historically) on product mix; the delayed railway dynamometer finally commissions by Aug-Sep 2026.
summary.business: Menon Bearings Limited manufactures engine bearings, bushes, thrust washers and strips (Bi-Metal division) serving OEM, aftermarket and export customers across commercial vehicles, tractors, two-wheelers, industrial engines and gensets. Its wholly owned subsidiary Menon Alkop Limited makes aluminium die-casting and precision-machined components for automotive, EV and hybrid platforms, while another wholly owned subsidiary, Menon Brakes Limited, makes asbestos-free brake linings for the domestic aftermarket and export markets.

currentContext.strengths: High profile customer base with diversified product distribution|Preferred supplier to all current OEMs|All manufacturing facilities under one roof|Strong, long-standing OEM relationships and integrated manufacturing capabilities across the group|Diversified product portfolio spanning engine bearings, aluminium die-casting and brake linings|Growing export footprint (~35% of FY26 revenue) across USA, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia
currentContext.strategies: Focus on niche, value-added and high-margin products as a competitive advantage|Expanding capacities across key divisions (Bi-Metal bearings, Braking systems, Alkop aluminium machining)|Increasing exports and strengthening global market presence (USA, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia)|Enhancing the product portfolio with high-margin, precision-engineered products|Continuing investments in sustainability and advanced manufacturing technologies|Exploring new opportunities in precision engineering, railways, defence, oil & gas and other industrial applications|Leveraging strong OEM relationships, integrated manufacturing capabilities and a diversified product portfolio for sustainable long-term growth|Expanding Menon Alkop's aluminium die-casting and machining capabilities, including entry into the EV component segment|Menon Brakes expanding export footprint and domestic aftermarket presence, and pursuing railway approvals|The Company declared and paid an interim dividend of Rs. 2/- per equity share (200% of paid-up equity share capital) on 5,60,40,000 equity shares of Re. 1/- each, declared on 25 July 2025 for the financial year ended 31 March 2026, noted by shareholders at the 35th AGM.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the Company commissioned and expanded advanced manufacturing capacities: Bi-Metal bearings capacity rose from 486 lakh units to 580 lakh units per annum (a 19% increase), and Braking Systems capacity expanded from 18 lakh pieces to 30 lakh pieces annually. Additional investments were undertaken for aluminium machining capacity expansion at wholly owned subsidiary Menon Alkop Limited, whose machining capacity was expanded by 40% during the year. At wholly owned subsidiary Menon Brakes Limited, a dynamometer installation is underway to secure railway approvals and OEM orders, with a significant turnover increase expected in FY26-27 following commissioning; Menon Brakes fully deployed capex of Rs. 0.58 crore in FY26, with a further Rs. 2.50 crore planned over the next two years. Going forward, the Company plans further investments in machining capacity, thrust washer production and advanced manufacturing capabilities, and continues to explore opportunities in precision engineering products, railways, defence, oil & gas and other industrial applications. The Company also invested in renewable and energy-efficient technologies during the year, including a rooftop solar power system with 3,870 kWp capacity, energy-efficient motors, LED lighting systems, electrically operated holding furnaces, and advanced boiler systems with pre-heat chambers.
currentContext.mdna: Engine bearing demand remains linked to ICE vehicle production, especially commercial vehicles, tractors and two-wheelers, plus steady aftermarket demand|Aluminium die-casting is gaining momentum across both ICE and EV segments due to lightweight and strength advantages that support fuel efficiency and emission reduction|Increasing regulatory standards, including BS-VI norms and stringent export requirements, are driving demand for high-quality precision-engineered components|The transition toward electric mobility may gradually impact demand for certain traditional components, but is simultaneously creating new opportunities in aluminium components, EV powertrain systems and structural applications|Government support through PLI schemes, FAME initiatives, Make in India and localisation policies is expected to support sector growth|India continues to attract global sourcing opportunities under the 'China Plus One' strategy|OEM production is expected to grow with increasing mobility demand and infrastructure-led rural development|Aftermarket segment supported by rising vehicle population and longer vehicle ownership cycles|Global tariff and geopolitical uncertainty has had a relatively limited impact on the Indian automotive sector due to localisation, GST rationalisation and stronger domestic supply chains|The Bi-Metal Division successfully developed and tested multiple high-value components for key customers, with substantial opportunities expected in both domestic and export markets|Growing demand for quality manufacturing has resulted in a higher number of RFQs for Menon Alkop Limited|Menon Alkop entered the EV segment through supply of components to global automotive platforms

risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices, particularly metals and energy costs, poses cost pressure; management flags 'volatile raw material situation, particularly metals' as a threat/future challenge, alongside constantly increasing operational costs that need to be nullified.

risks.risk: EV transition risk to traditional ICE-linked products
risks.note: The rapid transition toward electric mobility is reshaping the industry landscape; while this may gradually impact demand for certain traditional (engine bearing) components, it simultaneously creates new opportunities in aluminium components and EV powertrain systems.

Pricing pressure from OEMs and increasing customer expectations for cost optimization, combined with rising raw material costs and competitive pricing domestically and globally, pressures profitability.

risks.risk: Global geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and supply chain disruptions
risks.note: Global geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, and supply chain disruptions are flagged as a threat; the Company is also dependent on global economic conditions and international demand trends given its export exposure.

risks.risk: Technological adaptation and R&D investment burden
risks.note: Rapid technological advancements require continuous investment in R&D and manufacturing upgrades to keep pace with automotive technology and smart mobility solutions; failure to keep pace is flagged as a future challenge.

risks.risk: Capacity and workforce management during expansion
risks.note: Efficiently managing expansion plans while ensuring availability of skilled labour and technical expertise is flagged as a future challenge, including talent retention in Tier-II cities such as Kolhapur.
Meeting evolving emission norms, environmental standards, and safety regulations is flagged as a future challenge for the Company's operations.
Expanding aluminium die casting operations (Menon Alkop) without compromising quality, precision, or delivery timelines is explicitly flagged as a future challenge.

one-line thesis: Record quarter on every line — highest-ever Q1 sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT — with consolidated revenue +36.6% YoY to Rs 91.79 cr and PAT +67% (EPS Rs 2.52 vs Rs 1.50), achieved *despite* war-driven consumable inflation (carbide tools +300%) that they fully absorbed. The growth story is now explicitly export/China+1-led: a June US/Canada roadshow (Magna, Allison, Linamar) generated RFQs/NDAs worth an incremental Rs 65-75 cr over FY27-28, on top of a Rs 75 cr domestic RFQ pipeline (75-80% strike). Brakes surprised with 25% EBITDA (vs 12-14% historically) on product mix; the delayed railway dynamometer finally commissions by Aug-Sep 2026.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | Rs 91.79 cr | +36.6% | vs Rs 67.21 cr; total income +37.05%; **highest-ever Q1** |
| Revenue (standalone / bi-metal) | Rs 67.06 cr | +40.4% | vs Rs 47.76 cr |
| EBITDA (consol) | — | +57% | margin ~21.5-22% blended |
| PBT (consol) | Rs 18.51 cr | +67.4% | vs Rs 11.06 cr |
| PBT (standalone) | Rs 14.85 cr | +64.3% | vs Rs 9.03 cr; EBITDA +~60% |
| PAT (consol) | — | +67.35% | EPS Rs 2.52 vs Rs 1.50 |
| PAT (standalone) | Rs 11.23 cr | +63.5% | |
| Net debt | Internal accruals only | — | Capex funded fully by internal accruals, "no fresh loan" |
> Q1/Q2 are the seasonally *weak* half; Q3/Q4 historically stronger — so a +60% beat over last-year Q1 is management's internal benchmark being "crossed." Margin was achieved with raw-material prices up 20-25% (Cu/Al) fully passed through, plus 300% consumable (carbide) inflation *not* passed through — i.e. genuine operating leverage.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** FY27 guidance Rs 360 cr held (explicitly called "a conservative figure … we will stick to that"); could exceed on export momentum. Q4 "much better scenario" flagged.
- **3-year:** 20%+ YoY growth (conservative; "can be 25%"); **Rs 500 cr target pulled forward** from FY30 to "next 2-3 years."
- **Alkop (aluminium):** Rs 100 cr FY27 → Rs 125 cr FY28 (vs ~Rs 80 cr annualised run-rate).
- **Export mix:** rising to ~37% of revenue next year (from 24-30% historically).
- **Alkop EV share:** 8-10% by FY27-end (currently 4-5%).
- **Railway (brakes):** dynamometer commissioned by **Aug-end 2026**, technical rig running by Sep-end; RDSO/vendor-code registered; Rs 5-6 cr business year-1 → Rs 25-30 cr within 2 years.
- **New-order pipeline:** Rs 65-75 cr incremental from US/Canada (FY27-28) + Rs 75 cr domestic RFQ list at 75-80% strike → >Rs 60 cr additional this/next year. Africa direct: bearings/bushes/washers ~Rs 9 cr + brake linings Rs 6-7 cr/yr.
- **Capex:** Rs 9-10 cr bi-metal (FY27, +25-30% capacity, ~Rs 25 cr revenue potential) + Rs 4 cr Alkop; future capex asset-turn ~2.5x; all internal accruals.
order book & pipeline:
- **US/Canada (June roadshow):** RFQs/NDAs from Magna (9 aluminium plants in Canada, buys ~Rs 1,800 cr/yr), Allison Transmission, Linamar; incremental Rs 65-75 cr over FY27-28. US-based person hired to compress the 9-12 month realization to 6-7 months. Engine-bearing/bi-metal RFQs already converting (supply expected Q3-Q4 FY27); Alkop samples by CY2027.
- **Domestic:** Rs 75 cr RFQ list at various stages (feasibility→sample→PPAP→approval), 75-80% strike rate.
- **Europe:** Sept 2026 15-day visit (CNH/New Holland invited them to European suppliers; Netherlands offered business) — realization FY27-28.
- 37 parts already approved; 51 new parts under development.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Bi-metal (Bearings):** utilization ~80-87%; peak revenue capacity >Rs 400 cr on current machinery; single-source to John Deere >20 yrs; adding Rs 9-10 cr capex for +25-30% capacity. EBITDA margin 21%+.
- **Alkop (Aluminium die-casting):** realization risen to Rs 900+/kg (raw-material-driven; base ~Rs 700 at Rs 200-250 aluminium, now Rs 340-370); utilization 65-70%; EV customers TACO Prestolite, Tata Motors (Curvv/Punch EV), Eaton Concentric; moving to 1,600-ton HPDC parts. EBITDA ~21%.
- **Brakes:** 25% EBITDA this quarter (vs 12-14% historically) on product mix + halted low-margin Dubai/Africa exports; utilization 65-70%; entered 2W, entering 3W; railway + OEM optionality post-dynamometer.
growth verticals / optionality: China+1 / rupee-depreciation export capture (US, Canada, Europe, direct Africa); EV die-casting (Alkop 4-5%→8-10%); railway braking (Vande Bharat, metros, cargo/passenger bogies — dies already built); aerospace (Honeywell wheel parts, airport lighting — exploratory); secondary defence exposure via Allison washers (US). Not pursuing humanoid robotics or primary defence.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Integrated, high-value-add niche:** deliberately avoids commodity passenger-car bearings; focuses on heavy-duty tractor/engineering/industrial critical parts where value-add is higher and overheads minimal. Zero-PPM (parts-per-million rejection) certifications from multiple OEMs; OEE "up to global standards" → cost of production structurally lower, enabling reasonable pricing + margin.
- **30-40 yr sticky OEM relationships** (John Deere single-source >20 yrs; customers "older than me"); reliability/after-sales drives the next RFQ. Supported Allison through tariff period at margin cost — converted into more US RFQs. Third-generation promoter continuity.
margins & cost dynamics: Blended EBITDA ~21.5-22% (bi-metal > Alkop > brakes as the structural order, though brakes led at 25% this qtr on mix). Cu/Al up 20-25% and freight/consumables (carbide +300%) up sharply — Cu/Al passed through via indexing, consumables absorbed. Mgmt guides sustaining 20-21% blended; brakes to normalize toward 20% as low-margin exports resume.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Rs 9-10 cr bi-metal (+25-30% capacity) + Rs 4 cr Alkop this FY, modular/machinery-led — buildings already built (65,000 sq ft Alkop machine shop 50% occupied; 45,000 sq ft engine-bearing 50% occupied; ~7 acres spare land in aluminium plant). No land/greenfield needed for the next Rs 500 cr; scouting new bi-metal plot (Kolhapur/MIDC) for the 2+ year horizon. **Watch:** railway dynamometer commissioning (repeatedly delayed prior years) — now Aug-Sep 2026.
capital allocation: All capex via internal accruals; no fresh debt. Conservative "sustainable & secure business" posture — 100% advance required for new Africa merchant-export customers in first 6 months. No M&A named for bi-metal/Alkop (organic).
risks & watch-items:
- Monsoon/drought → tractor-segment softness (mgmt: "not worry," scrappage + govt capex offset).
- Geopolitics: Strait of Hormuz/West Asia war stalled merchant-export orders for ~3 months last quarter (now restarted); Rs 65-75 cr guidance is "subject to good monsoon and geopolitics not worsening."
- Dynamometer slippage risk on railway timeline.
- Raw-material timing gaps; consumable inflation not passed through.
- Brakes 25% margin flagged as mix-driven, may normalize.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular, promoter-led; transparent that brakes' 25% is product-mix (not to be annualized) and that Rs 360 cr is deliberately conservative. Track record of beating own guidance (Rs 270 cr target → delivered Rs 300 cr). Refused to give hard railway numbers pre-dynamometer ("don't want to give concrete numbers"). Grounded on defence ("very stringent … 2-3 years") and robotics ("different field, not exploring").
non-obvious takeaways:
- Alkop revenue can't be reverse-engineered from tonnage — Rs 900+/kg realization is raw-material-inflated, not volume; value-add is the real driver.
- The margin beat is *understated* quality: achieved while absorbing 300% carbide-tool inflation and with peak (Q3/Q4) seasonality still ahead.
- The Rs 500 cr target moving from FY30 to "2-3 years" is the biggest positive delta vs prior quarters.
- Infrastructure (buildings/land) already sunk for the next Rs 500 cr — incremental capex is only machinery at 2.5x asset-turn, so growth is high-ROCE.

management quality / tone: Confident, granular, promoter-led; transparent that brakes' 25% is product-mix (not to be annualized) and that Rs 360 cr is deliberately conservative. Track record of beating own guidance (Rs 270 cr target → delivered Rs 300 cr). Refused to give hard railway numbers pre-dynamometer ("don't want to give concrete numbers"). Grounded on defence ("very stringent … 2-3 years") and robotics ("different field, not exploring").
non-obvious takeaways:
- Alkop revenue can't be reverse-engineered from tonnage — Rs 900+/kg realization is raw-material-inflated, not volume; value-add is the real driver.
- The margin beat is *understated* quality: achieved while absorbing 300% carbide-tool inflation and with peak (Q3/Q4) seasonality still ahead.
- The Rs 500 cr target moving from FY30 to "2-3 years" is the biggest positive delta vs prior quarters.
- Infrastructure (buildings/land) already sunk for the next Rs 500 cr — incremental capex is only machinery at 2.5x asset-turn, so growth is high-ROCE.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
